newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Deals worth $150 million sealed at Tanzania forum.
newsitem.headline: Deals worth $150 million sealed at Tanzania forum.

text.p: Business deals worth more than $150 million have so far been signed at Tanzania's international investment forum, organisers said on Thursday.

"We've got 21 letters of intent and at least seven MOUs (memorandums of understanding) and joint ventures signed today," a senior U.N. official told Reuters, adding these deals were worth a total of $150 million and more was expected by Friday.

"Of meetings scheduled, 90 percent of the appointments have been kept and about 800 meetings held. Of course we would like to see more joint ventures signed but the forum has gone very well," added the official who declined to be named.
Most deals were in the power and mining sectors, senior conference sources told Reuters. The November 5-8 forum is the biggest gathering of investors in Tanzania's history.

Tanzanian officials see the forum as a key springboard for building investor confidence in Tanzania, one of the world's poorest countries, now trying to shake off the legacy of almost 30 years of debilitating socialist-inspired economic policies.
On Thursday, Swedish company Skanska International signed an $11.4 million deal for the first phase of underground mine development at a gold mine in northwest Tanzania.
